subject: physics
prompt: A heat engine is being designed to have a Carnot efficiency of 65.0% when operating between two energy reservoirs. If the temperature of the cold reservoir is 20.0°C, what must be the temperature of the hot reservoir?
newExplanation: Carnot efficiency is $\eta = 1 - T_c/T_h$ (temperatures in Kelvin). With $T_c = 293\text{ K}$ and $\eta = 0.65$: $0.65 = 1 - 293/T_h$, so $T_h = 293/0.35 \approx 837\text{ K} = 564^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: physics
prompt: If the terminals of a battery with zero internal resistance are connected across two identical resistors in series, the total power delivered by the battery is 8 W. If the same is connected across the same resistors in parallel, what is the total power delivered by the battery?
newExplanation: In series, $P = V^2/(2R) = 8\text{W}$, so $V^2 = 16R$. In parallel, the equivalent resistance is $R/2$, giving $P = V^2/(R/2) = 2V^2/R = 2(16R)/R = 32\text{W}$.

subject: physics
prompt: A series RLC circuit has a total impedance of 75.0 ohms. If the resistance is R=45.0 ohms and the average power delivered is P=352.8W, what is the RMS value of the AC voltage source?
newExplanation: From $P = I_{rms}^2 R$: $I_{rms} = \sqrt{352.8/45} = 2.8\text{A}$. Then $V_{rms} = I_{rms} Z = 2.8 \times 75 = 210\text{V}$.

subject: physics
prompt: An electron moving at 1.5x10^7 m/s enters a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude 2x10^-3 T, perpendicular to the field. The path is circular. What is the radius of the circular path?
newExplanation: For circular motion in a magnetic field, the magnetic force supplies centripetal force: $r = mv/(eB) = (9.11\times10^{-31} \times 1.5\times10^7)/(1.602\times10^{-19} \times 2\times10^{-3}) \approx 4.3\,\text{cm}$.

subject: physics
prompt: The cross-section areas of the small and large pistons of a hydraulic lift are 4.0cm^2 and 0.02m^2, respectively. What force must be applied to the small piston to lift a weight of 15,000N on the larger piston?
newExplanation: By Pascal's principle, pressure is transmitted equally, so $F_1 = W(A_1/A_2) = 15000 \times (4\times10^{-4}/0.02) = 300\text{N} = 3\times10^2\text{N}$.

subject: physics
prompt: A highway curve is banked so that a car at 13.5m/s can round it without skidding, without friction. If the banking angle is 30 degrees, what is the radius of the curve?
newExplanation: For a frictionless banked curve, $\tan\theta = v^2/(rg)$, so $r = v^2/(g\tan\theta) = 13.5^2/(9.8\times\tan 30^\circ) \approx 31.7\text{m}$.

subject: physics
prompt: A positive charge of 1.0×10⁻⁴C is on the negatively charged plate of a parallel plate capacitor. The top plate is at +10,000V and the bottom at -10,000V. How much work is required to move the charge from bottom to top plate?
newExplanation: Work to move a charge through a potential difference is $W = q\Delta V = 1.0\times10^{-4} \times 20{,}000 = 2.0\text{J}$ (the full 20,000V plate-to-plate difference, since the plates are at +10,000V and -10,000V).

subject: physics
prompt: What fundamental frequency can a string vibrate at if it is 30cm long and the velocity of traveling waves along the string is 120m/s?
newExplanation: For the fundamental mode of a string fixed at both ends, $f = v/(2L) = 120/(2\times0.30) = 200\text{Hz}$.

newExplanation: Stokes' law gives the viscous drag force on a sphere: $F = 6\pi\eta r v = 6\pi(0.985)(0.04)(2.5) = 0.591\pi\,\text{N}$.

subject: physics

subject: physics
prompt: Find the distance of the center of mass of the system (masses 3kg,3kg,3kg,2kg at positions 0,3,6,7m from A) from point A.

subject: physics
prompt: A large mass A (5kg) and small mass B (2kg) push apart; B moves away at 20m/s. What is the recoil velocity of A?
newExplanation: By conservation of momentum (starting at rest, total momentum stays zero): $5v_A + 2(20) = 0$, so $v_A = -8\text{m/s}$ — A recoils opposite to B's motion.

subject: physics
prompt: A rod PQ (length 1.8m) is attached at P to a wall. Weight W acts at 0.6m from P. The rod is kept horizontal by a wire to Q providing 50N at 30° to the horizontal. By taking moments about P, determine W.
newExplanation: Taking moments about P: the wire's torque is $F\sin(30^\circ)\times1.8$, balanced by $W\times0.6$. So $50\times0.5\times1.8 = 45 = 0.6W$, giving $W = 75\text{N}$.

prompt: Given the displacement vector $\mathbf{A} = (3\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j}) \, \mathrm{m}$, what is the unit vector in the direction of $\mathbf{A}$?

prompt: If the critical angle for an optically denser medium to air boundary is 53°, what will be the refractive index of the medium?

prompt: Two displacement vectors have magnitudes 4 m and 3 m. Which one of the following is NOT the possible value of the magnitude of their resultant vector?
newExplanation: The resultant of two vectors ranges from their difference to their sum: $|4-3|=1\text{m}$ to $4+3=7\text{m}$. Every option except $12\text{m}$ falls in that range, so $12\text{m}$ is the one that's not possible.

subject: physics
prompt: A train is moving along a straight line with a constant acceleration of 5 m/s 2 when it passes by a traffic light point. From there on, if the time taken by the train to reach a velocity of 30 m/s is 4 seconds, then what is the distance of the train from the traffic point after 8 seconds?
newExplanation: First find the velocity at the traffic light: $30 = v_0 + 5(4)$ gives $v_0 = 10\text{m/s}$. Distance after 8s from that point: $s = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2}at^2 = 10(8) + \frac{1}{2}(5)(8^2) = 80+160 = 240\text{m}$.

subject: physics

subject: physics

subject: physics
prompt: A tennis ball of mass 0.10 kg traveling horizontally at 40.0 m/s is struck back by a racket. If the ball returns back with a speed of 30.0 m/s in the opposite direction, what is the magnitude of the impulse delivered to the ball by the racket?
newExplanation: Impulse equals the change in momentum: $J = m(v_f - v_i) = 0.10\times(-30 - 40) = -7.0\,\text{kg·m/s}$ (taking the initial direction as positive) — magnitude $7.0\,\text{kg·m/s}$.
